meta.description: An Android music player for your own music, no subscriptions. Instructions, download and a guide to yt-dlp for downloading audio only.
hero.lead: Your MP3s are already yours. You don't have to pay anyone to listen to them. And nobody gets to spy on you while you listen.
install.title: Installing
install.step1: Download the APK with the button above, directly on your phone.
install.step2: Open it. Android asks you to allow installs from this source (browser or file manager): allow it, just this once.
install.step3: Updates install over the previous version: your mixtapes and settings are kept.
start.title: First launch
tabs.title: The tabs
tabs.mixtape: MIXTAPE: your playlists. Create, rename, burn. To move a track, long-press it, choose ↕ Move, use the ↑ ↓ arrows and press OK. Burning a mixtape doesn't touch your files.
volume.title: Even volume
volume.text: Each track is measured once (EBU R128, the same standard as ReplayGain 2.0) and played at -18 LUFS: no volume jumps between one MP3 and the next. Louder tracks are turned down, so raise your phone's volume a bit. You can turn it off in SETUP.
rules.title: House rules
rules.legal: Only download things that are yours or free to use: YouTube's terms forbid the rest.
yt.title: // yt-dlp ON THE COMPUTER
yt.needs.title: What you need
yt.needs.ffmpeg: FFmpeg: needed to convert to MP3 and for tags and covers.
yt.needs.deno: Deno: a JavaScript runtime yt-dlp uses to read YouTube. Without it, some videos give fewer formats or fail.
yt.eff.title: Audio only, efficiently
yt.eff.text: YouTube already has an audio track separate from the video: just take that (-f ba, “best audio”) and you never download the video. The most efficient thing is to keep it as it is, without re-converting:
yt.eff.m4a: M4A (AAC), no conversion: the fastest file to get, with no extra quality loss. ASD, Android, iPhone and almost all players can play it.
yt.eff.mp3: MP3 at 128 kbps: compatible with anything (old players, car radios), but it must be re-converted with FFmpeg, so it takes longer and loses a bit of quality. This is what the scripts below do.
yt.eff.one: Only the track, even if the link contains &list=:
yt.eff.some: Some tracks of a playlist (the 1st, the 3rd and the 5th to 7th):
yt.eff.archive: Re-download a playlist skipping the tracks already taken:
yt.eff.tags: Title, artist and cover inside the file:
yt.eff.cookies: If YouTube asks you to confirm you're not a bot, use your browser's login (close it first):
yt.eff.update: Keep it up to date: YouTube changes often and old versions stop working.
scripts.title: The scripts
scripts.url: scarica_url: paste a list of links (one per line) and it downloads them all, one at a time. If a link fails it moves on to the next and at the end tells you how many succeeded.
scripts.playlist: seleziona_playlist: paste a playlist link, it shows you the numbered list of tracks and you choose which to download (1,3,7-10 or tutti).

win.install_text: The easiest way: download installa_programmi.bat and double-click it. It uses winget, already included in Windows 10 and 11, to install yt-dlp, FFmpeg and Deno. Or by hand, from PowerShell:
win.manual: Without installing anything: download yt-dlp.exe and FFmpeg (from the zip take bin\ffmpeg.exe and bin\ffprobe.exe) and put them in the same folder as the scripts. The scripts find them on their own.
win.download_text: Each script needs two files in the same folder: the .bat (the one you double-click) and the .ps1 (the real script, in PowerShell).
win.run_text: Double-click the .bat. In scarica_url paste the links and press Enter on an empty line to start.
win.smartscreen: If Windows warns that the file comes from the Internet: More info → Run anyway, or right-click the file → Properties → tick Unblock. First, if you like, open them with Notepad: they're text, you can read everything they do.
